title: Pendulum

caveats: motion blur of ball near bottom of swing when moving fastest
2D animation with no calibrated real-world scale

slow_motion.evidence: no captions, no frame-rate effect and continuous motion indicate real-time playback

subjects.description: small round yellow ball hanging from a thin black string

observation.what_happens: A yellow ball on a black string swings side to side beneath a top mount against a chalkboard background. It starts high on the right and oscillates through the bottom centre to the left and back repeatedly, still swinging when the clip ends.

calibration.note: no ruler needed: the swing is measured as an angle

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth): hold g fixed and measure the pendulum's length L in metres from its swing
reasoning: Path is a circle of 440 px with 0.14 px error and theta spans +-1.04 rad (~60 deg), so large-angle pendulum geometry is needed with period ~2.3 s implying L~1.3 m. Peaks decay from 1.04 to 0.90 rad over 7.4 s, so undamped vs linear-damped vs quadratic-damped decay must be compared, plus a small-angle null model.

critique.finding: The ball swings on a string of length {L} pulled by gravity {g}. A gentle drag {gamma} slowly shrinks each swing.
critique.headline: Swinging ball slowly loses energy to gentle air drag.
critique.why_it_won: Linear drag keeps the swing size fading steadily, while quadratic drag lets later swings drift off.

headline: Swinging ball slowly loses energy to gentle air drag.
finding: The ball swings on a string of length 1.2 ± 7.08e-5 m pulled by gravity 9.81 m/s². A gentle drag 0.03 ± 1.27e-4 1/s slowly shrinks each swing.

eyeball.confidence: low - no absolute scale or timestamp; L from paper-sheet scale and pendulum geometry with T=2pi sqrt(L/g), gamma from near-constant peak amplitude
eyeball.law_in_words: Small-angle pendulum period T approx 2 pi sqrt(L/g) gives L from oscillation period, and damped peak amplitude envelope decays as exp(-gamma t /2).
